name: Processor D
justification: At the 1x fidelity optimum, Processor A needs 11 SWAPs and 33 routing two-qubit gates (81 total versus 48 logical), while Processor B embeds the ring with zero routing but needs 56 logical CX gates. Processor D uses a four-qubit cycle to remove ring routing and native RZZ gates to reduce the optimum circuit to 32 two-qubit gates at depth 57. We retain the official 0.001/0.005/0.01 rates because there is no measured evidence to claim better hardware. The accepted trade-off is assuming native RZZ has the same error rate as CX; the two-qubit tail does not help the ring, but enables a distance-4 Bell test.
